The '''1947–48 season''' was '''[[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' 45th season in existence and the club's [[La Liga|16th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
The season is best remembered as the worst league performance by the club in its history<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/laliga/20190111/454071291105/historias-liga-peor-liga-real-madrid.html|title=The worst league of Real Madrid|date=11 January 2019|accessdate=19 November 2020|language=Spanish|publisher=mundodeportivo.com|author=Jordi Subiran}}</ref> finishing on 11th spot avoiding relegation on the last round of the season<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/atletico-madrid/20190620/463010733379/llorente-el-duodecimo-que-pinta-rojo-en-la-camiseta-blanca.html|work=Marca|location=Spain|title=Llorente el 12th who painted red on his shirt|language=Spanish|date=20 July 2019|accessdate=15 July 2020}}</ref> in spite of a great campaign of midfielder [[Luis Molowny]] scoring nine goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.trescuatrotres.com/miguel-munoz-mucho-mas-que-flor/|publisher=trescuatrtres.com|title=Miguel Muñoz, more than a Flower|language=Spanish|date=9 October 2017|accessdate=15 July 2020}}</ref>

Real Madrid wore [[Squad number (association football)|squad numbers]] on their jerseys in the match against Atlético Madrid at the [[Estadio Metropolitano de Madrid]] on 23 November 1947, becoming the first team in La Liga to  do so.<ref>{{cite web |title=El primer equipo en lucir dorsales en su camiseta en la historia de la Liga |url=https://futbolretro.es/dorsales-por-primera-vez-en-liga/#:~:text=Aquel%20d%C3%ADa%20los%20jugadores%20madridistasSail%2C%20Clemente%2C%20Corona%2C%20Pont%2C,fueron%20los%2011%20jugadores%20que%20aline%C3%B3%20el%20Atl%C3%A9tico. |website=Futbolretro.es |access-date=17 July 2026 |language=es |date=12 January 2020}}</ref>

After three years of construction "[[Estadio Nuevo Chamartín|Nuevo Chamartín]]" (New Chamartín Stadium) was inaugurated on 14 December 1947 with a match between Real Madrid and the Portuguese side [[Os Belenenses]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120907115337/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1193040487651/1330073124892/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_to_play_1,500th_official_clash_at_the_Santiago_Bernabeu.htm?w=2|title="Real Madrid to play 1,500th official clash at the Santiago Bernabéu"}}. Real Madrid C.F.. Retrieved 22 November 2011</ref> The stadium had an initial capacity of 75,145 spectators.<ref>27,645 of which had seats, 7,125 covered and 47,500 for standing fans.</ref>

Meanwhile, the club fired two managers until [[Michael Keeping]] was signed for the second part of the season improving the path for the squad included a controversial 1–1 against top-league team [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid-atletico-madrid/2018/09/28/5bae1880e5fdea5f138b4621.html|title=Alsua goal with the hand in 1948:first controversial action in a Derbi|work=Marca|location=Spain|author=Fernando M. Carreño|date=28 September 2018|accessdate=20 November 2020}}</ref> The squad could reach a victory on 11 April 1948 against [[Real Oviedo]] 2–0 with a superb performance of Pruden saving Real Madrid from a relegation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/la-liga/real-madrid-evito-descenso-72-anos-victoria-agonica|title=Real Madrid passed relegation away 72 years ago |publisher=mediotiempo.com|date=11 April 2020|accessdate=2 November 2020|language=Spanish|author=José Andrés Díaz Lopez}}</ref>

The campaign was the first with numbered shirts (measure pioneered in Europe by [[Arsenal F.C.]] since 1928<ref>[https://www.directvsports.com/copa-mundial-fifa/noticias/que-mundial-empezaron-usarse-los-numeros-las-camisetas En qúe] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209123840/https://www.directvsports.com/copa-mundial-fifa/noticias/que-mundial-empezaron-usarse-los-numeros-las-camisetas |date=9 February 2019 }} on [[DirecTV Sports]], 14 June 2018</ref>) being the first match against local rivals [[Atlético Madrid]] with a 0–5 result.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/11/24/mas_futbol/1479971225_282428.html|title= We Won by a 'Ortiz' −0 score|date=24 November 2016|accessdate=20 November 2020|author=Alfredo Relaño|publisher=as.com|language=Spanish}}</ref>

After saving the category, the team was eliminated in the round of 16 of the [[1947–48 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]] by [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], losing the two matches of the series.
